title: Freightos Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results, Cuts Adjusted EBITDA Loss by Over 50% and Announces a Share Repurchase Program
summary: Barcelona – Freightos Limited (NASDAQ: CRGO), the leading vendor-neutral global freight pricing, booking and procurement platform, today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. “Our third quarter results demonstrate continued execution against the priorities we established earlier this year: strengthening operational discipline, improving our cost structure, and modernizing our offering to support […]
body_markdown:
- *Record Revenue of $7.8 Million, with Platform Momentum Exceeding Expectations*
- *Cost Optimization Plan Announced in March Reaches $4.8 Million Annualized Savings, Exceeding Original $4.5 Million Target*
- *Company Announces $1.7 Million Share Repurchase Program*


Barcelona – Freightos Limited (NASDAQ: CRGO), the leading vendor-neutral global freight pricing, booking and procurement platform, today reported financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.


“Our third quarter results demonstrate continued execution against the priorities we established earlier this year: strengthening operational discipline, improving our cost structure, and modernizing our offering to support long-term growth,” said Pablo Pinillos, CEO of Freightos. “We have delivered the cost savings we targeted, significantly narrowing our Adjusted EBITDA loss as we approach breakeven. At the same time, platform transactions grew 15% year-over-year, driven primarily by customers using our software solutions, demonstrating the strength of our integrated model. By embedding our solutions into our customers’ daily workflows , we are driving platform adoption and increasing the value of our network. We are also making tangible progress in modernizing our offering to improve customer value and scalability. Importantly, we remain well capitalized to fund our plans while returning capital to shareholders through share repurchases. Together, these achievements put us in a stronger position to pursue our long-term growth opportunities with greater financial flexibility.”


## Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights


- Revenue of $7.8 million for the third quarter of 2026, up 2% compared to $7.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.
- IFRS Gross Margin of 67.4%, compared to 69.1% in the third quarter of 2025. Non-IFRS Gross Margin of 73.3%, compared to 74.8% in the third quarter of 2025.
- IFRS loss of $2.3 million, compared to $5.0 million for the third quarter of 2025.
- Adjusted EBITDA of negative $1.3 million, compared to negative $2.6 million in the third quarter of 2025, representing a 52% year-over-year reduction in Adjusted EBITDA loss, driven by cost savings.
- Cash and cash equivalents and short-term bank deposit balance at the end of September 2026 stood at $22.3 million.


## Recent Business Highlights


- **Transactions Growth:** Q3 2026 transactions totaled 494 thousand, up 15% year-over-year and above management’s expectations. Transaction growth was driven primarily by customers using Freightos’ software solutions, reflecting the expanding reach of Freightos’ global booking network, and the growing contribution of integrated software solutions to customer engagement and platform utilization.
- **Carrier Growth:** 79 carriers were active (receiving more than five transactions each) on the Platform in Q3 2026, compared with 75 in Q2 2026 and 77 in Q3 2025. Freightos’ extensive carrier connectivity and growing buyer participation strengthen the value of its vendor-neutral network, bringing more choice, greater efficiency and broader digital access to international freight markets. Among the carriers active in the quarter were Korean Air, which recently joined the platform, as well as certain carriers that fell below the five transactions threshold in the second quarter.
- **Unique Buyer Users:** The number of unique buyer users digitally booking freight services across the platform grew to approximately 21,900, up 6% year-over-year compared to approximately 20,600 in Q3 2025 and 21,000 in Q2 2026.
- **Gross Booking Value (GBV) Record:** The total value of transactions processed on the Freightos Platform reached a record $437 million in Q3 2026, up 30% year-over-year and above management’s expectations. GBV demonstrates the scale of freight commerce flowing through Freightos’ digital infrastructure. For Q3 2026, GBV also reflected elevated freight rates amid tighter capacity and higher fuel costs.
- **Revenue Performance:** Third quarter revenue was led by solid momentum across Freightos for Forwarders eBooking, customs clearance solutions, and market intelligence data, underscoring the diversification and complementary strengths of the product portfolio. Total Platform revenue in the third quarter of 2026 was $3.0 million, up 16% year-over-year, and Solutions revenue was $4.8 million, down 6%.
- **Product: Solutions Modernization:** Earlier this month, Freightos announced the launch of the next generation of Freightos for Forwarders. The platform advances Freightos’ established digital commerce and workflow capabilities into an intelligent, AI-native freight orchestration network that unifies rates, quoting, booking, and market intelligence in one connected environment. Freightos views the launch as an important milestone and believes it will support future growth in its Solutions business.

## Share Repurchase Program


The Freightos Board of Directors has authorized a share repurchase program of up to $1.7 million of its ordinary shares. The authorization reflects the Board’s and management team’s confidence in the company’s underlying fundamentals, business strategy, and long-term cash flow generation profile. Management believes the program represents an attractive, accretive investment opportunity to enhance long-term shareholder value while continuing to fund core business growth. Under the authorization, repurchases may be executed periodically through open-market purchases in accordance with Rule 10b-18, privately negotiated transactions, or pursuant to Rule 10b5-1 trading plans, in compliance with applicable securities laws. The timing, volume, and pricing of repurchases will depend on prevailing market conditions, liquidity requirements, and alternative capital allocation priorities. The program does not obligate Freightos to acquire any specific dollar amount or number of shares, and it may be suspended, modified, or discontinued at any time at management’s discretion.

## Glossary


- **Transactions:** Number of bookings for freight services, and related services, placed by Buyers across the Freightos platform with third-party sellers and with Clearit. Sellers of transactions include carriers (airlines, ocean liners and LCL consolidators) and also other providers of freight services such as trucking companies, freight forwarders, general sales agents, and air master loaders. The number of transactions booked on the Freightos platform in any given time period is net of transactions that were canceled prior to the end of the period. Transactions booked on white label portals hosted by Freightos are included if there is a transactional fee associated with them.
- **Carriers:** Number of unique air and ocean carriers, mostly airlines, that have been sellers of transactions. For airlines, we count booking carriers, which include separate airlines within the same carrier group. We do not count dozens of other airlines that operate individual segments of air cargo transactions, as we do not have a direct booking relationship with them. Carriers include ocean less-than-container load (LCL) consolidators. In addition, we only count carriers when more than five bookings were placed with them over the course of a quarter.
- **Unique buyer users:** Number of individual users placing bookings, typically counted based on unique email logins. The number of buyers, which counts unique customer businesses, does not reflect the fact that some buyers are large multinational organizations while others are small or midsize businesses. Therefore, we find it more useful to monitor the number of unique buyer users than the number of buyer businesses.
- **GBV:** Total value of transactions on the Freightos platform, which is the monetary value of freight services and related services contracted between buyers and sellers on the Freightos platform, plus related fees charged to buyers and sellers, and pass-through payments such as duties. GBV is converted to U.S. dollars at the time of each transaction on the Freightos platform. This metric may be similar to what others call gross merchandise value (GMV) or gross services volume (GSV). We believe that this metric reflects the scale of the Freightos platform and our opportunities to generate platform revenue.
- **Adjusted EBITDA:** Loss before income taxes, finance income, finance expense, share-based compensation expense, depreciation and amortization, reorganization expenses and change in fair value of warrants.
- **Platform revenue:** Fees charged to buyers and sellers in relation to transactions executed on the Freightos platform. For bookings conducted by importers/exporters, our fees are typically structured as a percentage of booking value, depending on the mode and nature of the service. When freight forwarders book with carriers, the sellers often pay a pre-negotiated flat fee per transaction. When sellers transact with a buyer who is a new customer to the seller, we may charge a percentage of the booking value as a fee.
- **Solutions revenue:** Primarily subscription-based SaaS and data. It is typically priced per user or per site, per time period, with larger customers such as multinational freight forwarders or enterprise shippers often negotiating fixed, all-inclusive subscriptions. Revenue from our Solutions segment includes certain non-recurring revenue from services ancillary to our SaaS products, such as engineering, customization, configuration and go-live fees, and data services for digitizing offline data.


## About Freightos


Freightos® is the leading digital infrastructure platform powering the international freight industry. Operating as a vendor-neutral network, Freightos connects airlines, ocean carriers, trucking carriers, freight forwarders, and importers and exporters of all sizes to bring transparency, efficiency, and resilience to global supply chains.


The Freightos platform digitalizes freight execution by transforming manual, fragmented processes into seamless, connected, and data-driven digital workflows. Freightos delivers integrated capabilities including procurement, pricing, quoting, booking, customs clearance, payments, and market intelligence across air, ocean, and road freight. By serving as the intelligence middleware layer that unifies data and workflows, Freightos empowers smarter operational decisions and enables market participants to transact, collaborate, and manage global shipments more effectively.


Used by thousands of logistics service providers and businesses around the world, Freightos combines software, network connectivity, transaction infrastructure, and market data into an interconnected digital ecosystem.
